exposure: intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy (ICP) status (including asymptomatic hypercholanemia of pregnancy (AHP))
cohort: The study included 957 pregnant individuals with C-ICP (Chinese Intrahepatic Cholestasis of Pregnancy) who delivered and had regular antenatal examination records from a hospital in Guangzhou, China.
finding: The risk of adverse perinatal outcomes, including preterm birth, meconium-stained amniotic fluid, and admission to the neonatology department, increased significantly with higher maternal total bile acid (TBA) concentrations in patients with C-ICP.
